chunks.heading: Details of each Segment
chunks.text:
During the week (06th Mar 2025 – 12th Mar 2025), deficient rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 68%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01th Mar to 12th Mar 2025) is lower than LPA by 34%. Rainfall Forecast: 13th Mar – 19th Mar 2025 a) A Western Disturbance impacted Western Himalayan States, North West India and North East India during the week. b) Under the influence of these systems, fairly widespread to widespread light/moderate rainfall/snowfall accompanied with thunderstorm & lightning likely over Arunachal Pradesh and scattered to fairly widespread light/moderate rainfall/snowfall accompanied with thunderstorm, lightning & gusty winds (speed 40-50 kmph) likely over Assam & Meghalaya and Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram & Tripura during 13th-17th March. c) No significant weather likely over rest parts of the country during the week.
| 4 20th Mar - 26th Mar, 2025 d) Under the influence of western disturbances, scattered to fairly widespread rainfall/snowfall is likely over Western Himalayan Region during some days of the week. e) Light/moderate isolated to scattered rainfall is also likely over east & northeast India and south Peninsular & adjoining central India during some to many days of the week. f) Overall, rainfall is likely to be above normal over south Peninsular India & adjoining central India and below normal over rest parts of the country during the week.

chunks.heading: 2. TEMPERATURE: MIN & MAX
chunks.text:
Temperature Forecast 13th Mar – 19th Mar 2025 a) No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over plains of Northwest India during next 24 hours and fall by 2-3°C thereafter. b) No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over central India during next 2 days and fall by 2-3°C thereafter. c) Gradual fall in maximum temperatures by 2-4°C likely over many parts of West India during the week. d) Gradual rise in maximum temperatures by about 2-3°C likely over East India during 1st half of the week and no significant change thereafter.
| 5 e) Gradual rise in maximum temperatures by about 2-4°C likely over many parts of south peninsular India during the week. 20th Mar - 26th Mar, 2025 f) Maximum temperatures are likely to be above normal by 2-4°C over most parts of northwest India and by 2-3°C over most parts of East India; near normal over Gujarat and parts of northeast India. g) There is low to moderate probability of heat wave conditions over south Rajasthan,Gujarat and Odisha during some days of the week. h) Minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal or near normal over most parts of the country.
| 6

rainfall/snowfall is likely over Western Himalayan Region during some days of the week.
e) Light/moderate isolated to scattered rainfall is also likely over east & northeast India and
south Peninsular & adjoining central India during some to many days of the week.
f) Overall, rainfall is likely to be above normal over south Peninsular India & adjoining
central India and below normal over rest parts of the country during the week.
